text.p: Vice President Kocheril Raman Narayanan was elected India's 10th president on Thursday, an Election Commission spokesman said.

Narayanan, the first member of a low Hindu caste to be voted president of the world's biggest democracy, was backed by Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front coalition, the Congress party and the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.

The 76-year-old former diplomat was elected by an electoral college comprising 4,848 lawmakers of the federal parliament and state legislatures who voted in a secret ballot across the nation through a system of proportional representation.
The new president, scheduled to take office for a five-year term on July 25, will take charge three weeks before the 50th anniversary of India's independence from Britain on August 15.

Traditionally a largely ceremonial job, the post of the president, India's constitutional head, has been seen as crucial following the emergence of coalition politics in which the head of state can play a key role in the formation of governments.
President Shankar Dayal Sharma's five-year term expires on July 25. Although eligible for a second term, Sharma did not seek re-election.
